payload.prompt: Which statements correctly describe the Azure Speech-to-Text SDK?

options.text: It is a client library for converting spoken audio into written text.
options.rationale: Correct. The SDK packages ready-made client code for speech recognition. Its main role is converting audio input into text output.

options.text: It helps applications talk to Azure Speech without writing every service call from scratch.
options.rationale: Correct. A client library simplifies communication with a service or API. The Speech-to-Text SDK makes recognition easier to add to applications.

options.text: It mainly converts written text into spoken audio.
options.error_type: confuses STT with TTS
options.rationale: That describes text-to-speech, not speech-to-text. Speech-to-text starts with audio and returns written text.
options.better_fit: This is correct for the Azure Text-to-Speech SDK.

options.text: It is only a visual testing page for speech features.
options.error_type: confuses SDK with playground
options.rationale: The SDK is code used by applications. A visual playground is a separate testing environment for trying capabilities before coding.
options.better_fit: This is closer to the Foundry playground used for experimentation.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The SDK is ready-made code for adding audio-to-text recognition to apps.

payload.prompt: Which tasks can the Speech-to-Text SDK handle for an application?

options.text: Send microphone, file, or stream audio to Azure Speech securely.
options.rationale: Correct. The SDK can work with several audio sources and send them to Azure Speech. Secure communication is part of the integration it supports.

options.text: Receive recognized text in near real time or after processing completes.
options.rationale: Correct. The SDK returns transcription results during live-style recognition or after processing. This lets apps support both immediate and completed transcript workflows.

options.text: Select a synthetic voice and speaking pitch for generated audio.
options.error_type: confuses STT responsibilities with TTS responsibilities
options.rationale: Voice and pitch settings belong to speech synthesis. They do not describe the core job of a speech-to-text SDK.
options.better_fit: This is correct for text-to-speech output configuration.

options.text: Replace all application logic with an automatic user interface.
options.error_type: overstates SDK responsibilities
options.rationale: The SDK handles service communication and recognition-related plumbing. Developers still write application logic and user interface behavior.
options.better_fit: This would fit a fully hosted product interface, not a client library.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The SDK handles audio transport and transcript results while developers build the app logic.

options.text: Use SpeechSynthesizer to choose the input stream
options.error_type: confuses synthesis object with recognition flow
options.rationale: SpeechSynthesizer is for producing audio from text. It does not choose or process an input stream for speech recognition.
options.better_fit: This fits a feature that speaks text back to the user after the text is available.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would configure output speech while the stream still would not be recognized.
feedback.instructional: Use recognition objects such as SpeechRecognizer with AudioConfig for speech-to-text input.

options.text: Skip sending audio to Azure Speech models
options.error_type: omits cloud recognition analysis
options.rationale: The program flow depends on Azure speech models analyzing the audio. If the app never sends or streams audio, it cannot receive recognized text from the service.
options.better_fit: This fits an offline-only recorder that stores audio without transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: The UI would have no recognized text to update because no recognition processing occurred.
feedback.instructional: A speech-to-text flow must connect, provide audio, and receive recognition results.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Streaming recognition needs configuration, audio input, and update handling.

payload.prompt: A small business wants an app that turns saved voicemail recordings into readable messages. Which implementation choices best match that app pattern?

options.text: Specify the endpoint, key, and audio source for the saved voicemail
options.rationale: Correct. A voicemail transcription app needs connection details and the voicemail audio source. Those inputs allow the app to send the recording for recognition.

options.text: Use a SpeechRecognizer object to transcribe and display the text result
options.rationale: Correct. SpeechRecognizer is the object used to recognize speech and produce text results. Displaying those results gives reviewers readable messages.

options.text: Use SpeechSynthesizer to generate each voicemail
options.error_type: confuses transcribing voicemails with creating spoken audio
options.rationale: SpeechSynthesizer generates audio from text. Saved voicemails already contain audio and need text output instead.
options.better_fit: This fits an app that reads written customer messages aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The business would create spoken audio but still lack transcripts of the saved voicemails.
feedback.instructional: Voicemail transcription uses recognition because the starting material is recorded speech.

options.text: Use Voice Live as the only path because voicemail is always a live conversation
options.error_type: confuses saved recordings with live voice sessions
options.rationale: Voicemail recordings are stored audio, not active two-way conversations. Voice Live is unnecessary when the goal is simply to transcribe saved messages.
options.better_fit: This fits a real-time assistant that listens to callers and speaks back immediately.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would be designed for live interaction instead of reviewing stored messages.
feedback.instructional: Match the tool to the workflow: saved voicemail review is an audio-to-text recognition task.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The voicemail pattern uses connection values, an audio source, and SpeechRecognizer to display text.

flashcards.back: A client library that turns spoken audio into written text.
Endpoint and authentication settings for Azure Speech.
The microphone, audio file, or stream input.
Use SpeechRecognizer to transcribe and display text.
